scope: LibreCAD_3 persistence compile compatibility with the current upstream libdxfrw public headers
classification: consumer-build-configuration incompatibility; not a format-support result

source_revisions.librecad3: local dirty checkout; CMake reports branch fix/msvc-eigen-include, commit 132265a0

observations.fact: The project sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD to 17 and the dxfrw target publishes cxx_std_17 as a PUBLIC compile feature.
The consumer sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD to 14 with CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED enabled.

The persistence target compiles with -std=gnu++14 and includes upstream libdxfrw headers from /Users/dli/dev/libdxfrw/src. The probe supplied raw include/library paths, not the exported dxfrw target, so its PUBLIC compile feature was not propagated.

reproduction.build_result: failure while compiling persistence/file.cpp and persistence/libdxfrw/dxfimpl.cpp; public headers report no std::optional or std::nullopt under C++14, followed by cascading type errors

interpretation: The observed failure is explained by the consumer compile mode and does not establish a source/API defect under the libdxfrw target's declared C++17 requirement. The repository AGENTS.md description of libdxfrw as C++14 is stale relative to CMakeLists.txt and must not be used as the current build contract.
implementation_follow_up: Prefer the installed CONFIG package in LibreCAD_3 with CMAKE_FIND_PACKAGE_PREFER_CONFIG=ON and libdxfrw_DIR set to the selected package, or update its module-mode imported interface target to publish cxx_std_17. Do not pass raw source include/library variables without a compile-feature contract.
The CONFIG-package path now configures, builds persistence, and passes the existing focused export (3/3) and planar open/save/reopen (1/1) controls against the installed package archive.
Keep the default module-mode failure, clean consumer revision, full application, ABI, and Linux/Windows qualification as separate remaining P8 gates.
limitations: The LibreCAD_3 checkout is dirty and was not modified; prior custom runners were reused, and DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES verified that they loaded the newly built persistence/kernel dylibs.
No native application, ABI, Windows, or Linux qualification was performed.
